approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill creates rules for companies that distribute cash in Australia so that cash remains available for people who need it.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission and the Reserve Bank of Australia would run the new system, including crisis management powers for the RBA.

The explanatory memorandum says the bill gives the RBA power to deal with crises in cash distribution and sets up dispute resolution and service standards, but does not give start dates or thresholds.
Creates a legislative framework for cash distribution services.
Introduces a crisis management and resolution regime for critical cash distribution services.
Gives the ACCC information gathering and enforcement powers.
Gives the RBA new crisis readiness and resolution powers.
Sets up a designation process for cash distribution services.
Provides for oversight of service agreements and access agreements.
Companies and organisations that distribute cash in Australia.

Original question agreed to. Bills read a second time. I will now deal with the committee-of-the-whole amendment circulated by the Australian Greens. The question is that the amendment to the Cash Distribution Framework Bill 2026 on sheet 3967 be agreed to. _Australian Greens' circulated amendment—_ (1) Page 164 (after line 4), after Subdivision A, insert: Subdivision AA — Protections for employees 162A Powers must not be exercised to lessen employee entitlements The Reserve Bank must not take action in accordance with this Part in relation to a designated entity if: (a) the action would result in the entitlements of an employee of the designated entity being less beneficial than they were immediately before the action was taken; or (b) each of the following are satisfied: (i) there is an employee (the _current employee_) of the designated entity immediately before the action is taken; (ii) the action would result in the engagement of a person (the _new employee_) to perform the same, or substantially the same, work as that performed by the current employee; (iii) the entitlements of the new employee would be less beneficial than the entitlements of the current employee.

Moved the Cash Distribution Framework (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2026 for second reading, stating it would support implementation of the broader framework, maintain access to cash services, and give the ACCC interim transitional powers to help ensure continuity during implementation.

Presented the Selection of Bills Committee's eighth 2026 report and moved its adoption, recommending referrals of multiple bills to Senate committees with specified reporting dates; subsequent amendments proposed excluding the Regulatory Reform Omnibus Bill and referring the National Self-exclusion Register levy bill for inquiry.

Declared that, unless otherwise ordered, the Cash Distribution Framework Bill 2026 and its consequential amendments and transitional provisions bill stood referred to the Federation Chamber for immediate further consideration.

Moved second reading of the Cash Distribution Framework Bill 2026 and related consequential amendments bill, proposing Reserve Bank designation powers, ACCC oversight, service standards, dispute resolution and crisis funding of up to $400 million to maintain cash access; debate was adjourned and resumed consideration was ordered for a later hour.

Supported the Cash Distribution Framework Bill 2026 as a belated response to market concentration after the Armaguard-Prosegur merger, endorsing ACCC regulation and emergency arrangements while arguing that bank branch closures and cash acceptance, including at pharmacies, also require action; moved an amendment citing the 2027 moratorium end date and concerns about delay.

As President, put the question on Senator Canavan's second reading amendment and an Australian Greens committee amendment to the Cash Distribution Framework Bill 2026 that would bar the Reserve Bank from exercising its powers over a designated entity in a way that reduces employee entitlements, before the bill was read a second and third time and passed.
